meta.label: Peak-month visitors per resident (2024)
meta.methodNote: The comune's busiest month's tourist-accommodation nights spent (presenze), divided by the number of days in that month, divided by the comune's resident population (comuni.json, most recently published year — one year newer than this metric's own 2024 tourism figures, a real vintage mismatch). Reads as: on an average night in this comune's busiest month, this many overnight tourists are present for every resident — 0.16 means 16 tourists per 100 residents, so the night-time population is 1.16 times the resident one (it is a ratio of visitors to residents, not a multiplier of the population). Registered commercial accommodation only, set against the residents of the whole comune, so a large comune with a small tourist core reads lower than its busiest streets feel. Same source and year-selection reasoning as the seasonality index above.
meta.coverageNote: ISTAT discloses monthly tourist-accommodation arrivals/presenze for only 2470 of Italy's ~7,900 comuni — a comune with too few (or zero) registered accommodation establishments has no row at all, for statistical-confidentiality reasons the source states explicitly, not a gap this site introduced. This measures REGISTERED commercial tourist accommodation only — a comune whose seasonal population swing comes from private second homes rather than hotels/B&Bs will not show up here even if that swing is real. A further 68 disclosed comuni are excluded because their ISTAT code in this source doesn't match a current comuni.json id — mostly Sardinia towns (Alghero, Arzachena, Olbia, Porto Torres, Santa Teresa Gallura, Sassari and others) listed under an old province grouping this file hasn't updated, plus Castegnero's pre-merger code — excluded rather than guessed at, a real coverage gap worth noting for readers researching Sardinia specifically.
